label: input token d at original positions 1-4
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is the letter d during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions t=1..4. It never fires on d at t=0 or at t>=5, never on other tokens, and essentially never in the delimiter/copy phase (55 stray copy-phase activations at t=5). Magnitude depends on position: highest at t=2 (top examples are all "m o d", ~1.94), high at t=1 (~0.8 of max), moderate at t=3 (~0.65 of max), and weak at t=4 (~0.2-0.26 of max, lowest quartile). Preceding tokens, sequence length, and whether d is a repeat do not gate it (a repeated d at t=4 still fires weakly). Dev F1 0.9996.

issues: The claims hold up. On the test split precision is 1.0 (0 false positives), recall is 0.9992, F1 is 0.9996 and mass recall is 0.9999. Every d at t=1-4 fires, so repeated d's at t=4 fire too.

The 53 test misses (55 on dev) form a tiny pattern, not noise. They are all L=3 sequences with d at original position 1, where the d copied back as input at step 5 (recall_idx 2) fires very weakly (about 0.03-0.12 of max). They hold 0.0% of the activation mass, so they are negligible. The explanation already notes them as copy-phase activations at t=5.

The magnitude ordering matches the dev profile. Active counts per t are similar (16.7k, 16.7k, 16.2k, 13.7k) and mass shares are 0.308 / 0.369 / 0.249 / 0.074. That gives relative means of about 0.83 / 1 / 0.69 / 0.24, consistent with the claimed t=2 peak, t=1 high, t=3 moderate and t=4 weak.
There are no activations on any non-d token, at t=0, at t>=6, or in the delimiter phase. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
